question.leadin: Answer the following about "dreams" in American history.
question.text: Mahalia Jackson prompted this civil rights leader to "Tell them about the dream" during his "I Have a Dream" speech as part of the March on Washington.
question.clue: Robert Kennedy's impromptu speech in Indianapolis following this man's death probably kept the city from rioting.

swap.leadin: This Supreme Court case overturned the "separate but equal" doctrine of Plessy v. Ferguson.
swap.text: Name this case, in which the Court unanimously ruled that segregation in schools was unconstitutional.
swap.clue: This case's decision cited an experiment in which children were asked to choose between dolls by Kenneth and Mamie Clark.

question.text: As president, Johnson launched this series of programs that included Medicare and Medicaid. Its most famous part was the "War on Poverty" that led to the Economic Opportunity Act.
question.clue: Sargent Shriver helped found a program that focused on early childhood education as part of this initiative, and another of its programs provided health insurance to citizens over the age of 65.

swap.text: This future Supreme Court justice argued before the Court for the NAACP in Brown v. Board of Education.
swap.clue: His victories in Sweatt v. Painter and McLaurin v. Oklahoma State Regents opened up college access to previously disenfranchised applicants.

question.text: This California governor unsuccessfully sought the 1952 Republican nomination for President. He was named Supreme Court Chief Justice and presided over landmark cases such as Brown v. Board and Miranda v. Arizona.
question.clue: As a popular governor of California, he became the losing running mate of Thomas Dewey in 1948.

swap.text: The White Night Riots took place after the assassination of this first openly gay elected official in the United States, who was shot along with George Moscone by Dan White.
swap.clue: This man's death inspired Cleve Jones to begin the NAMES Project.

question.leadin: He escalated US involvement in Vietnam after claiming falsely that a second Gulf of Tonkin incident occurred.
question.text: Name this Texan who signed the Civil Rights Act of 1964 after succeeding John F. Kennedy.
question.clue: During a speech at the University of Michigan, this president announced an initiative that produced a program supporting low-income children called Head Start.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the election of 1972.
swap.text: This candidate had to bow out of the Democratic party after he was shot by an assassin. He had earlier declared "segregation now, segregation tomorrow, segregation forever."
swap.clue: During this man's 1972 presidential run with former Air Force general Curtis LeMay, he was shot and paralyzed by Arthur Bremer.

question.text: Modified by the "loss of liberty" standard in Argersinger v. Hamlin, it drew on Powell v. Alabama. For 15 points, name this case that incorporated the "right to counsel" clause of the Sixth Amendment, guaranteeing an attorney to anyone accused of a state felony.
question.clue: Future Supreme Court Justice Abe Fortas was appointed to represent the plaintiff in this case, who was arrested in Panama City, Florida for breaking into a pool hall.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about Abe Fortas.
swap.text: Fortas was nominated to be Chief Justice by this president, but the nomination was withdrawn due to scandal.
swap.clue: In one campaign, this politician used the slogan "In your guts, you know he's nuts'' against an opponent, and released an ad depicting a young girl picking daisies before a nuclear bomb explodes.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the intersections of sex and politics.
question.text: In 1982, California politician John Schmitz admitted to fathering a baby out of wedlock, which effectively ended his career. Schmitz was the 1972 presidential nominee of the American Independent Party, which in 1968 nominated this conservative for the presidency with running mate Curtis LeMay.
question.clue: This long-time Alabama governor who orchestrated his "stand in the schoolhouse door" to protest wildly unpopular desegregation at his state's flagship university. He ran for president in 1968 with Curtis LeMay.

swap.leadin: This type of fee was eliminated in federal elections by the 24th amendment.
swap.text: What two-word term is used to refer to any fee required before a person is allowed to vote?
swap.clue: A Supreme Court case filed by Annie Harper made these things illegal at the state level in 1966, a year after they were made illegal at the federal level.

question.leadin: Answer the following about people or things disliked by former senator Strom Thurmond.
question.text: Thurmond led the Senate effort to defeat the nomination of this man as Chief Justice. This jurist earlier served as the defense attorney in the case of Gideon v. Wainwright.
question.clue: When Lyndon Johnson tried to elevate him to Chief Justice, a filibuster by a bipartisan coalition in the Senate forced the President to withdraw his nomination. He later resigned from the Court after a financial scandal.

swap.leadin: This work responded to an open letter penned by eight clergymen titled "A Call for Unity," which cautioned against "outsiders coming in."
swap.text: Name this text, which draws on Augustine in arguing that "injustice anywhere is a threat to justice everywhere."
swap.answerHtml: “Letter from Birmingham Jail” [or “Letter from a Birmingham Jail” or “Letter from Birmingham City Jail” or “The Negro is Your Brother”]
swap.clue: It was written in response to the statement "A Call for Unity" that urged the use of the court system rather than "direct action" led by outsiders.

question.text: The 1948 case Morgan v. Virginia earlier outlawed segregation in some of these places. The segregation of these places was fully ruled unconstitutional in the case Browder v. Gayle.
question.clue: The caseBrowder v. Gayledealtwith the desegregation of these things, whichare operatedby Trailways and Greyhound.

swap.leadin: In 1964, three members of this organization were brutally murdered in Neshoba County, Mississippi.
swap.text: Name this civil rights organization that, as a part of the COFO, led the campaign to register African-American voters in Mississippi in Freedom Summer. This organization's founding Chicago chapter desegregated White City Roller Rink and fought overcrowding and double-shifts in public schools.
swap.clue: Its second director retired in order to design a planned town called Soul City in North Carolina which quickly fell through.

question.text: The Green Book helped develop this network of theaters and nightclubs catering to black audiences in the South. Similar to the Jewish Borscht Belt, it launched the careers of B.B. King, Ray Charles, and Marvin Gaye.
question.clue: During Jim Crow, black performers traveled to nightclubs such as the Uptown Theatre in Philadelphia that were part of this informal set of venues, whose name is a play on the Borscht Belt.

swap.leadin: It was decided in 1950 and was argued by WJ Durham and Thurgood Marshall.
swap.text: Identify this case where the Supreme Court held that the University of Texas Law School had to provide a substantially equal education to the black plaintiff and, thus, had to admit him.

question.leadin: This book argues that its main character divided society into elite "Franklins" who were resented by the striving middle-class "Orthogonians."
question.text: Name this book by Rick Perlstein that analyzes the "fracturing of America" during the 1960s through the rise of the title politician.
question.answerHtml: Nixonland [or Nixonland: The Rise of a President and the Fracturing of America]

swap.text: This one-time leader of the NAACP spoke at the Prayer Pilgrimage. Under his leadership, the NAACP helped black-owned businesses get loans in the South by backing the Tri-State Bank, and he eventually stepped down in 1977.
swap.clue: This activist was leader of the NAACP from 1955 to 1977, succeeding Walter White. He had earlier edited W.E.B. Du Bois's The Crisis magazine, and was known for opposing militancy in the civil rights movement.
